microtheory.name: developmental_psychology
microtheory.definition: Systematic changes in cognition, emotion, behaviour across the lifespan. Piaget's stages, Vygotsky's social development, Bowlby + Ainsworth's attachment, Erikson's psychosocial stages, Kohlberg's moral development. Substrate analogue: the substrate's developmental loop + critical periods + babble-as-grounding map directly to developmental constructs.

concepts.name: piaget_sensorimotor_stage
concepts.definition: 0-2 years. Infant constructs understanding via sensory experience + motor action. Object permanence emerges ~8mo. Substrate analogue: substrate's babble-as-grounding stage — building world model via action + observation.

concepts.name: piaget_preoperational_stage
concepts.definition: 2-7 years. Symbolic thought + language; egocentric; centration; lacks conservation. Substrate analogue: substrate with symbolic representation but no meta-cognition.

concepts.name: piaget_concrete_operational_stage
concepts.definition: 7-11 years. Logical operations on concrete objects; conservation; classification + seriation. Substrate analogue: substrate using rules on specific Mt content but not yet abstract reasoning.

concepts.name: piaget_formal_operational_stage
concepts.definition: 12+ years. Abstract + hypothetical reasoning. Some never reach. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-cognitive layer (ArchitectureCortex + DevelopmentCortex) reasoning over its own Mts.

concepts.name: assimilation
concepts.definition: Piaget. Integrating new info into existing schemas. Schema stays; info adapts. Substrate analogue: adding concepts to existing Mt without restructuring.

concepts.name: accommodation
concepts.definition: Piaget. Modifying schemas to fit new info. Schema changes. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt restructuring under sustained disconfirmation — the slow learning mode.

concepts.name: zone_of_proximal_development
concepts.definition: Vygotsky. Gap between what a child can do alone vs with help. Learning happens in this zone. Substrate analogue: substrate's adjacent-possible Mt extensions — what feature_invention can construct from current concepts.

concepts.name: scaffolding
concepts.definition: Wood + Bruner + Ross 1976. Skilled other provides graduated support that fades as learner takes over. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded Mts + corrections that bootstrap capability before plasticity_override decays.

concepts.name: private_speech
concepts.definition: Vygotsky. Children's external self-talk that gradually internalises into thought. Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree composition externally manipulated → internalised into reflexes.

concepts.name: cultural_mediation
concepts.definition: Vygotsky. Cognition develops via culturally-provided tools (language, math notation, etc.). Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded vocabulary IS its cultural mediation.

concepts.name: attachment_theory
concepts.definition: Bowlby + Ainsworth. Early caregiver-infant bond shapes lifelong relational templates. Strange Situation: secure / insecure-avoidant / insecure-anxious / disorganised. Substrate analogue: substrate's initial seed Mts shape its lifetime drive patterns.

concepts.name: secure_attachment
concepts.definition: Caregiver responsive + available. Child explores from secure base, distressed at separation, comforted at reunion. Substrate analogue: substrate with stable foundation Mts + drive-balance allowing exploration.

concepts.name: insecure_avoidant_attachment
concepts.definition: Caregiver rejecting/unavailable. Child suppresses attachment needs. Substrate analogue: substrate with collapsed curiosity drive — exploration suppressed by past failures.

concepts.name: insecure_anxious_attachment
concepts.definition: Caregiver inconsistent. Child amplifies attachment signals. Substrate analogue: substrate's hyperactive coherence drive — over-allocating to identity protection.

concepts.name: internal_working_model
concepts.definition: Bowlby. Mental representation of self + others + relationships, built from attachment experiences. Influences adult relationships. Substrate analogue: substrate's self_concept Mt + identity_field bias.

concepts.name: erikson_trust_vs_mistrust
concepts.definition: 0-1 yr. Resolved by consistent caregiving → basic trust. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational coherence drive — early successes establish whether the world is predictable.

concepts.name: erikson_autonomy_vs_shame
concepts.definition: 1-3 yr. Resolved by allowing self-direction → autonomy. Substrate analogue: substrate's early curiosity-drive — whether exploration is reinforced.

concepts.name: erikson_initiative_vs_guilt
concepts.definition: 3-6 yr. Resolved by encouraging initiative → purpose. Substrate analogue: substrate's emergent goal-formation capability.

concepts.name: erikson_industry_vs_inferiority
concepts.definition: 6-12 yr. Resolved by competence experiences → industry. Substrate analogue: substrate's accumulated mastery via successful ActionSpec dispatch.

concepts.name: erikson_identity_vs_role_confusion
concepts.definition: 12-18 yr. Resolved by integrating multiple roles → identity. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-integration into coherent self_concept.

concepts.name: kohlberg_preconventional_morality
concepts.definition: Pre-adolescence. Avoid punishment, gain reward. Substrate analogue: substrate's RPE-driven correction firing — direct reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: kohlberg_conventional_morality
concepts.definition: Adolescence. Conform to social norms + laws. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded Rules as moral constraints.

concepts.name: kohlberg_postconventional_morality
concepts.definition: Few adults. Reason from abstract principles that may override conventional rules. Substrate analogue: substrate's derivation_mechanism + ArchitectureCortex reasoning from foundational principles.

concepts.name: perceptual_narrowing_psychological
concepts.definition: Specialisation of perception during sensitive periods. Infants discriminate all phonemes / all faces; pruned to native ones by ~12 mo. Substrate analogue: substrate's predicate pruning + Mt specialisation.

concepts.name: fast_mapping
concepts.definition: Carey + Bartlett 1978. Children learn new word meaning from a single exposure. Substrate analogue: substrate's single-shot Concept addition into existing Mt scaffold.

concepts.name: joint_attention
concepts.definition: 12-18 mo. Sharing focus on an object with another person. Foundation of language + theory of mind. Substrate analogue: in collaborative multi-substrate contexts, shared Mt focus.

concepts.name: object_permanence
concepts.definition: Piaget. Understanding that objects exist when not perceived. Develops ~8 mo. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent Mt state across input gaps.

rules.name: stages_unfold_in_fixed_order
rules.head: the substrate develops cognitive capabilities over time
rules.body: earlier stages must complete before later ones can begin. Piaget's invariant sequence. Substrate's foundational Mts must be installed before meta-Mts can run.

rules.name: learning_happens_in_zone_of_proximal_development
rules.head: the substrate is positioned to learn a new capability
rules.body: the new capability must be 1 step beyond current — too easy = no growth, too far = no scaffold. Vygotsky. Substrate's curiosity-drive should target adjacent-possible Mt extensions.

rules.name: attachment_style_persists_into_relational_templates
rules.head: the substrate's early seed-Mt experiences
rules.body: shape its lifetime drive ensemble + relational expectations. Bowlby's internal working model. Substrate's foundational Mts as relational template.

rules.name: sensitive_periods_have_open_then_close_dynamics
rules.head: specific learning capabilities
rules.body: are time-windowed; if missed, very hard or impossible to acquire later. Genie's case. Substrate's plasticity_override decay window.

rules.name: fast_mapping_via_existing_scaffold
rules.head: the substrate encounters a new concept that fits an existing Mt
rules.body: it integrates with one exposure. Carey + Bartlett 1978 — substrate's single-shot Concept addition into scaffold-rich domains.

rules.name: scaffolding_supports_then_fades
rules.head: an external system supports the substrate in acquiring a capability
rules.body: the support should gradually decrease as the substrate internalises the capability. Wood + Bruner + Ross 1976 — substrate's plasticity_override decays as Mt structure stabilises.
